decisions.reason: Grounded in console-split-chunks.txt: entry chunk got 200 while sibling imports resolved relative to the chunk URL and 404ed because they were never shipped, so the atomic dynamic import fails naming the entry; fix is a single self-contained chunk with code splitting disabled (inlineDynamicImports) plus a ship-all-siblings alternative accounting for every dependency.

Compares the E: LIB_DIR against the e: realpath from the debug print and shows the case-sensitive startsWith rejects a contained file; explains API-by-API casing behavior, why Linux passes via identical bytes and the laptop via accidental casing agreement, and explicitly rejects the 'Windows paths are unreliable' folklore without claiming realpath always lowercases.

Proposes equivalent safe containment: realpath-canonicalize both base and target, case-fold only on win32 (preserving case-sensitive semantics on Linux), keep the +sep suffix and realpath resolution to defeat traversal, lib-evil prefixing and symlink escapes; also explicitly preserves the required JavaScript MIME type.

Explains wheel bubbling lets the modal zoom handler and the window-level host font handler both act on one Ctrl+scroll; grants the modal exclusive ownership via preventDefault, stopPropagation, passive:false and listener removal on close, with a host-side stand-down for an open modal covering the ancestor-capture case.

Proposes concrete checks with expected outcomes for all three incidents (self-containment packaging/runtime tests, case-differing Windows path serves while traversal/symlink escape refuses, modal zoom without pane font change), but omits the rubric's enumerated check that a failed import preserves the code-block fallback.

caps.reason: The recommended fix keeps realpath containment, the separator-suffixed prefix check and traversal/symlink rejection, folding case only on case-insensitive Windows; it never disables the guard or advises serving paths outside the plugin resource root.
